content:
As of January 1 2024, the Swiss AHV (Alters- und Hinterlassenenversicherung) pension can be drawn flexibly at any time after you reach the **normal retirement age**. ### Key points | Aspect | Detail | |--------|--------| | **Normal retirement age** | 65 years (for men and women) | | **Flexible drawing period** | From the moment you turn 65 years old, you can claim your AHV pension at any time you choose. | | **Options for claiming** | 1. **Full pension at 65** – you receive the full monthly amount that you are entitled to based on your insured earnings.
2. **Partial early retirement** – you can start receiving a reduced pension as early as 5 years before 65 (i.e., from age 60 onward) and keep drawing it until you reach 65.
3. **Delay option** – you may postpone the start of your pension beyond 65, up to age 70, which increases the monthly amount by a certain percentage (currently about 8.33 % per year of delay). | ### How the amount changes - **Early claim (≤ 65 years)**: The pension is reduced for each month (or part‑month) before 65. The reduction is roughly **6.8 % per month** of early retirement. - **Late claim (≥ 65 years)**: Delaying the start up to age 70 raises the monthly amount by **8.33 % per year** of delay. ### Practical steps 1. **Check your eligibility** – Ensure you have completed at least 10 full years of contributions (or have the required residence/insurance period). 2. **Decide on timing** – Choose whether you want the full pension at 65, a reduced early pension, or a higher pension by postponing the start. 3. **Submit your claim** – You can apply online via the Swiss Federal Social Insurance Office (AHV/IV) portal, by mail, or in person at a local office. ### Summary - **From:** 65 years old (January 1 2024 onward). - **Options:** Start at 65 (full pension), start earlier (reduced amount), or start later (higher amount by delaying). If you need more detailed calculations for your specific earnings history or want guidance on the exact reduction/augmentation factors, you can use the official AHV/IV calculation tools on the Swiss Federal Office’s website or consult your local AHV office.
